perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information:

- He is a project manager and believes his project team is unmotivated and underperforming; this makes him frustrated, anxious, and worried.
- He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with his friend Arthur Begum, a police officer, to seek advice.
- He heard Arthur say that motivation is tricky, that Harold should understand what drives each team member individually, and that one-on-one conversations can help people feel valued and understood.
- Harold decided to try Arthur’s advice and felt hopeful and relieved.
- In a team meeting, Harold told the team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it.
- Harold planned to schedule individual meetings with each team member.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He discussed this with Arthur. He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of one-on-one meetings to uncover underlying issues.
- In those meetings, Harold asked team members about concerns. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making it hard to stay motivated.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts, would consider redistributing tasks to ease pressure, and said their well-being was important to him.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance, and intended to create a more supportive, open team environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He told the team about these planned changes. He heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help them work better together, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed.
- Harold told the team their input and well-being were crucial to success and encouraged them to work together to make the project a success.

Harold does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, unspoken motives, narrator-only descriptions of their personalities or backgrounds, or events he did not observe or hear about.
